title: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (October 2026) — the corridor's unstacked HMI morning, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: IR: the publisher's own forward calendar — nahb.org/news-and-economics/housing-economics/indices/nahb-wells-fargo-housing-market-index-release-dates fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 47,131 bytes), whose "2026 HMI Schedule" table carries the standing note "Normal release time: 10:00 AM Eastern Time" and the row "Oct. 2026 | October 19, 2026". NAHB produces this series, so this promotes on the same precedent as the sibling nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 (the identical table), existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 (NAR's own calendar) and challenger-job-cuts-2026-09-03. Corroborated three ways this session, all primaries: (1) NAHB's live HMI page, /indices/housing-market-index (HTTP 200, 61,518 bytes), whose "HMI Key Findings: August 2026" block reports index 35, current sales 39, six-month expectations 43, buyer traffic 23, 35% of builders cutting prices at an average 6% reduction and incentives at 63% — the edition NAHB's own schedule dates 2026-08-17; (2) the same schedule page recovered from TEN web.archive.org snapshots (20211021, 20220928, 20230906, 20240227, 20240616, 20241023, 20250322, 20250617, 20251012 and the live fetch), yielding 84 publisher-authored dates for 2020-2026 — an independent snapshot set from the sibling lane's, which nonetheless reproduces its 84-date series exactly; (3) 78 of the 80 already-elapsed scheduled dates are US trading sessions, and the mid-month Mon/Tue convention is unbroken across those seven years. Caution recorded rather than smoothed: the only two exceptions are 2023-06-19 and 2024-06-19, both Juneteenth market holidays, so a scheduled date is NAHB's commitment and not a guarantee the tape is open. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The October edition, filed by the nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 lane as the UNSTACKED CONTROL for the one caution its own instance could not clear, and this session resolves that caution with a primary. The proposal said the October 2026 G.17 date was unverified because federalreserve.gov/releases/g17/g17_release_dates.htm 404s (it still 404s as of 2026-09-06). The Board's maintained table lives at releases/g17/release_dates.htm — with the underscore — and was fetched direct this session (HTTP 200, 117,098 bytes, 334 dates 2000-2027, 'Last Update: August 18, 2026', with October 2025 and November 2025 still reading NA from the funding lapse). Its row reads 'October 2026 | 16-October-2026', and the Board's announcements feed (feeds/g17.html, HTTP 200, 614,006 bytes) says verbatim: 'In 2026, the G.17 release on Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization will be published at 9:15 a.m. on January 16, February 18, March 16, April 16, May 15, June 15, July 17, August 18, September 18, October 16, November 17, and December 16.' So the 09:15 industrial-production print lands the FRIDAY BEFORE this HMI, not on it. 2026-10-19 is genuinely unstacked: the October stack has fully cleared (CPI and the Beige Book 10-14; PPI, retail sales and MTIS 10-15; import/export prices, G.17, opex and the Treasury primary-dealer agenda 10-16), the FOMC blackout runs 10-17 through 10-29 so no Fed speaker competes, and nothing this calendar tracks is dated 2026-10-19 at all. It is also the trading day immediately before New Residential Construction on 2026-10-20 (Census's own historic_release_dates.xls, HTTP 200, 55,808 bytes, 510 dates 1984-02-16 -> 2026-12-17), the 91.0% D-1 pattern again, and the first session after October monthly opex. What this session measured on the class 2026-10-19 belongs to. The sibling's magnitude null holds and tightens: on the 44 UNSTACKED HMI days, ITB open->close reads 0.9894% against a 0.9689% clean baseline (p=0.91), XHB 0.9437% vs 0.8696% (p=0.65), SPY gap 0.3391% vs 0.3275% (p=0.85). The paired sentiment-vs-data test is newly SPLIT by stacking — 39 of the 71 consecutive-session HMI->starts pairs are unstacked, and on them ITB's sentiment day is the smaller mover 18 times out of 39 (46.2%, sign p=0.75). Giving the sentiment print the morning to itself changes nothing, which is exactly what the control was proposed to establish. Two instance confounds were checked and are inert: Monday HMI days (n=25) read 0.9514% vs 0.9604% (p=1.00), and the 14 post-opex HMI days 1.0742% vs 0.8654% (p=0.35). One genuinely NEW and non-null finding, the first this event's research has produced, and it closes the residual the sibling flagged as untestable. NAHB's own Table 2 National HMI History (t2-national-hmi-history-202608.xls, HTTP 200, 35,840 bytes, 500 monthly readings 1985-01 -> 2026-08) supplies the print series the sibling could not reach. Across the 78 release days, the HMI's month-over-month change correlates with the SAME-DAY SIGNED ITB open->close: r=+0.2557, permutation p=0.0292; XHB corroborates at r=+0.2193 (p=0.0569); SPY does not, r=-0.0587 (p=0.59) — the homebuilder-specific pattern a real channel would produce and a market-wide artefact would not. It is NOT tradeable and the ledger says so three ways: sign agreement is 54.8% (40/73, p=0.48), on the unstacked class it is 48.8% (20/41, p=1.00) and the correlation there is r=+0.2389 at p=0.117, and a month-over-month delta is not a surprise-versus-consensus, so co-movement with the conditions the survey measured cannot be separated from a reaction to the 10:00 release without intraday data this runner does not have. `symbols: []` and `impact: low` are re-derived here, not inherited. Date is `confirmed` on the publisher's own calendar; that licenses nothing, and the call is stand aside on every horizon.
